name: Proliferating Trichilemmal Cyst

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Proliferating Trichilemmal Cyst

criteria.description: Presence of lobulated cystic lesion with trichilemmal keratinization and abrupt keratinization without granular layer
Solitary, slowly enlarging scalp nodule typically on the vertex or occipital region
Positive staining for cytokeratin markers consistent with outer root sheath differentiation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of trichilemmal keratinization with compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from squamous cell carcinoma is critical due to potential for local aggressiveness

imaging: Ultrasound showing well-defined hypoechoic cystic lesion with internal echoes
MRI may show lobulated cystic mass with variable signal intensity
other: Histopathology demonstrating trichilemmal keratinization without granular layer

distinguishingFeatures: Invasive growth pattern with cellular atypia
Presence of keratin pearls and atypical mitoses on histology
Presence of granular cell layer in cyst wall

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of scalp lesion
references: Lever's Histopathology of the Skin, 11th Edition
Journal of Cutaneous Pathology, Proliferating Trichilemmal Tumors: A Clinicopathologic Study
